examples.label: Query all the names of all calendars:
examples.xml_code:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<fmxmlsnippet type="FMObjectList">
  <Step enable="True" id="141" name="Set Variable">
    <Value>
      <Calculation>While( 
[ 
	names = ""; 
	// query list of Calendar IDs
	list = MBS( "Calendar.Calendars" ); 
	count = ValueCount(list); 
	index = 1
] ; 
	index ≤ count ; 
[ 
	id = GetValue(list; index); 
	// query name for each ID
	name = MBS( "Calendar.Calendar.GetTitle"; id); 
	names = names & name & ¶; 
	index = index + 1 
] ; 
// return all the names
names )</Calculation>
    </Value>
    <Repetition>
      <Calculation>1</Calculation>
    </Repetition>
    <Name>$r</Name>
  </Step>
</fmxmlsnippet>

functions.name: Calendar.Item.SetPriority
functions.description: Sets the priority of a task/reminder. The iCalendar specification allows priority to be specified with an integer in the range of 0-9, with 0 representing an undefined priority, 1 the highest priority, and 9 the lowest priority. When a user sets the priority to high, medium or low in iCal saves the priority as 1, 5, or 9 respectively. Clients are encouraged to use these values when setting a task's priority, but is is possible to specify any integer value from 0 to 9. In iCal, a task with a priority in the range of 1-4 will show up as high priority, a task with a priority of 5 will be displayed as having medium priority, and 6-9 will be  displayed as having a low priority.

# And sync back changes
#
# Please adjust to your fields and your special use case!
# You can optimize to only update fields on each side if changed
#
Go to Record/Request/Page [First]
Loop
# Check if we have an ID for this todo already
If [
ToDos::SyncUID
≠ ""]
Set Variable [
$c
; Value:
ToDos::SyncUID
]
#Query last modification date
Set Variable [
$completed
; Value:
MBS
( "
Calendar.Item.GetCompleted
";
ToDos::SyncUID
)]
Set Variable [
$datum
; Value:
MBS
( "
Calendar.Item.GetDateStamp
";
ToDos::SyncUID
)]
If [
MBS
("isError")]
# Reminder was deleted, so we recreate
Set Field [
ToDos::SyncUID
; ""]
Commit Records/Requests [No dialog]
Else
#Update
If [
$datum
>
ToDos::Last_Change
]
#

#
#Sync note field
Set Variable [
$notes
; Value:
MBS
( "
Calendar.Item.GetNotes
";
ToDos::SyncUID
)]

ToDos::To
Do Main Text  ≠
$notes
]
#Special: If note starts with # then move number to duration field

$notes
); 1) = "#"]
Set Variable [
$duration
; Value:GetAsNumber ( LeftWords (
$notes
; 1 ))]

ToDos::To

$duration

Else

ToDos::To

$notes

$title
; Value:

$title

functions.name: Calendar.Notification.Evaluate
functions.description: Installs a notification evaluation. This expression is evaluated whenever something in the calendar database changed.

parameters.name: Expression
parameters.description: The expression to evaluate.

functions.name: Calendar.Notification.GetChangedExternally
functions.description: Queries if the last notification script call was caused by a changed in another app. If this function returns zero, the change was made by your own FileMaker solution. This property is not always set by the OS for all changes, especially with some sync services.

functions.name: Calendar.Notification.GetDeletedRecords
functions.description: Queries list of deleted records. Only valid in a notification script. Please note that the plugin may not be able to provide information for deleted record contents. Valus in this list are IDs of calendars, events, or reminders, depending on the notification (See Calendar.Notification.GetWhat ). If all three lists (updatedRecords, DeletedRecords, InsertedRecords) are empty, that indicates everything has changed, and the client should refresh the calendar, event, and reminder information currently being used. Since this tends to be an expensive and inconvenient operation, it will only occur under unusual circumstances, such as when restoring from backup.

functions.name: Calendar.Notification.GetInsertedRecords
functions.description: Queries list of inserted records. Only valid in a notification script. Valus in this list are IDs of calendars, events, or reminders, depending on the notification (See Calendar.Notification.GetWhat ). If all three lists (updatedRecords, DeletedRecords, InsertedRecords) are empty, that indicates everything has changed, and the client should refresh the calendar, event, and reminder information currently being used. Since this tends to be an expensive and inconvenient operation, it will only occur under unusual circumstances, such as when restoring from backup.

functions.name: Calendar.Notification.GetProcessID
functions.description: Queries the process ID. In a notification script you can use this function to learn who made the change for external changes. For notifications caused by your own solution, this value may be undefined.

functions.name: Calendar.Notification.GetProcessName
functions.description: Queries the process name. In a notification script you can use this function to learn who made the change for external changes. For notifications caused by your own solution, this value may be undefined.

functions.name: Calendar.Notification.GetUpdatedRecords
functions.description: Queries list of updated records. Only valid in a notification script. Valus in this list are IDs of calendars, events, or reminders, depending on the notification (See Calendar.Notification.GetWhat ). If all three lists (updatedRecords, DeletedRecords, InsertedRecords) are empty, that indicates everything has changed, and the client should refresh the calendar, event, and reminder information currently being used. Since this tends to be an expensive and inconvenient operation, it will only occur under unusual circumstances, such as when restoring from backup.

functions.name: Calendar.Notification.GetUserUID
functions.description: Queries the user ID. In a notification script you can use this function to learn who made the change for external changes. For notifications caused by your own solution, this value may be undefined.

functions.name: Calendar.Notification.GetWhat
functions.description: Queries what changed in the database. Can be "Calendars", "Reminders" or "Events". In a notification script you can use this function to learn what changed and what IDs the functions Calendar.Notification.GetUpdatedRecords , Calendar.Notification.GetDeletedRecords and Calendar.Notification.GetInsertedRecords return.

functions.name: Calendar.Notification.Set
functions.description: Installs a notification script. This script is called whenever something in the calendar database changed. It can be useful to just call this function without a script name just to have the plugin watch for changes in calendar and clear it's cache. With plugin version 6.0 or newer the script name can be a script ID number. In that case the plugin queries the script name for the given script ID. This allows to call scripts by ID and avoid problems if scripts are later renamed. Notice: FileMaker 19.2 adds a fmplugin extended privileges. If you have such an extended privileges to allow the plugin to trigger scripts, you need to grant permissions for it. If such a privilege is not defined, the plugin is allowed to trigger scripts. See FileMaker product documentation for details.

parameters.name: FileName
parameters.description: The name of the FileMaker File that contains the script.

parameters.name: ScriptName
parameters.description: The name of the script to run.

#
Go to Record/Request/Page [First]
Loop
# Check if we have an ID for this todo already

ToDos::SyncUID
≠ ""]
Set Variable [
$c
; Value:
ToDos::SyncUID
]

$completed
; Value:

Calendar.Item.GetCompleted
";
ToDos::SyncUID

Set Variable [
$datum
; Value:

( "
Calendar.Item.GetDateStamp
";
ToDos::SyncUID
)]
If [
MBS
("isError")]
# Reminder was deleted, so we recreate
Set Field [
ToDos::SyncUID
; ""]
Commit Records/Requests [No dialog]
Else

If [
$datum
>
ToDos::Last_Change
]
#

; Value:

Calendar.Item.GetNotes
";
ToDos::SyncUID

ToDos::To
Do Main Text  ≠
$notes

#Special: If note starts with # then move number to duration field

$duration

$notes

functions.name: CLGeocoder.Cancel
functions.description: Cancels a pending geocoding request. You can use this method to cancel a pending request and free up the resources associated with that request. Canceling a pending request causes the completion handler block to be called. If the request is not pending, because it has already returned or has not yet begun, this method does nothing.

functions.name: CLGeocoder.GeocodeAddressString
functions.description: Submits a forward-geocoding request using the specified string. This method submits the specified location data to the geocoding server asynchronously and returns. Your completion handler block will be executed on the main thread. After initiating a forward-geocoding request, do not attempt to initiate another forward- or reverse-geocoding request. Geocoding requests are rate-limited for each app, so making too many requests in a short period of time may cause some of the requests to fail. When the maximum rate is exceeded, the geo coder passes an error back. You need to use CLGeocoder.Close later to free the geo coder. Seems to not work on server as it always times out.

parameters.name: Address
parameters.description: A string describing the location you want to look up. For example, you could specify the string "1 Infinite Loop, Cupertino, CA"” to locate Apple headquarters.

parameters.name: Wait
parameters.description: Pass 1 to wait for geocoder to have a result. Pass 0 to not wait and check later if geocoder is done.

examples.label: Query in one let statement and return JSON or error:
examples.xml_code:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<fmxmlsnippet type="FMObjectList">
  <Step enable="True" id="141" name="Set Variable">
    <Value>
      <Calculation>Let ( [
	Address = "Berlin, Germany";
	// run query and wait a bit
	g = MBS( "CLGeocoder.GeocodeAddressString"; Address; 1 );
	e = MBS("IsError");
	// query JSON if we got something
	r = If (e = 0; MBS( "CLGeocoder.JSON"; g ); g);
	// free resources
	f = If (e = 0; MBS( "CLGeocoder.Close"; g ); 0)
]; r )</Calculation>
    </Value>
    <Repetition>
      <Calculation>1</Calculation>
    </Repetition>
    <Name>$r</Name>
  </Step>
</fmxmlsnippet>

functions.name: CLGeocoder.ReverseGeocodeLocation
functions.description: Submits a reverse-geocoding request for the specified location. This method submits the specified location data to the geocoding server asynchronously and returns. Your completion handler block will be executed on the main thread. After initiating a reverse-geocoding request, do not attempt to initiate another reverse- or forward-geocoding request. Geocoding requests are rate-limited for each app, so making too many requests in a short period of time may cause some of the requests to fail. When the maximum rate is exceeded, the geo coder passes an error back. You need to use CLGeocoder.Close later to free the geo coder. CoreLocation geo coder reference numbers are starting at 24000 and counting up for each new geo coder. Seems to not work on server as it always times out.

parameters.name: Latitude
parameters.description: The latitude of the coordinate.

parameters.name: Longitude
parameters.description: The longitude of the coordinate.

parameters.name: Wait
parameters.description: Pass 1 to wait for geocoder to have a result. Pass 0 to not wait and check later if geocoder is done.

examples.label: Reverse geocode location:
examples.xml_code:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<fmxmlsnippet type="FMObjectList">
  <Step enable="True" id="141" name="Set Variable">
    <Value>
      <Calculation>MBS("CLGeocoder.ReverseGeocodeLocation"; CLGeocoder::Latitude; CLGeocoder::Longitude)</Calculation>
    </Value>
    <Repetition>
      <Calculation>1</Calculation>
    </Repetition>
    <Name>$r</Name>
  </Step>
</fmxmlsnippet>

examples.label: Run query and get back JSON or error:
examples.xml_code:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<fmxmlsnippet type="FMObjectList">
  <Step enable="True" id="141" name="Set Variable">
    <Value>
      <Calculation>Let ( [
	latitude = 52.517631899999998;
	longitude = 13.4096574;
	// run query and wait a bit
	g = MBS( "CLGeocoder.ReverseGeocodeLocation"; latitude; longitude; 1 );
	e = MBS("IsError");
	// query JSON if we got something
	r = If (e = 0; MBS( "CLGeocoder.JSON"; g ); g);
	// free resources
	f = If (e = 0; MBS( "CLGeocoder.Close"; g ); 0)
]; r )</Calculation>
    </Value>
    <Repetition>
      <Calculation>1</Calculation>
    </Repetition>
    <Name>$r</Name>
  </Step>
</fmxmlsnippet>

functions.name: CNContact.AddPostalAddress
functions.signature: MBS( "CNContact.AddPostalAddress"; ContactIdentifier { ; Label; Street; City; State; postalCode; Country; ISOCountryCode; subLocality; subAdministrativeArea } )
functions.description: Adds an postal address to a contact. This is a convenience function to add just one postal address account with a given label to the contact. Please call CNContactStore.UpdateContact later to store the values.

parameters.name: ContactIdentifier
parameters.description: The contact identifier.

parameters.name: Label
parameters.description: The label to use. For your convenience we translate Work, Home and Other to the right values, so they get localized in display. Default label is Other.

parameters.name: Street
parameters.description: The street name with house number.

parameters.name: City
parameters.description: The city name.

parameters.name: State
parameters.description: The name of the state.

parameters.name: postalCode
parameters.description: The postal code.

parameters.name: Country
parameters.description: The name of the country.

parameters.name: ISOCountryCode
parameters.description: The ISO country code.

parameters.name: subLocality
parameters.description: The sub locality. Only used on MacOS 10.12.4 or iOS 10.3 and newer.

parameters.name: subAdministrativeArea
parameters.description: The sub administrative area. Only used on MacOS 10.12.4 or iOS 10.3 and newer.

functions.name: CNContact.AddPostalAddressJSON
functions.description: Adds an postal address to a contact with JSON. This is a convenience function to add just one postal address account with a given label to the contact. Please call CNContactStore.UpdateContact later to store the values. The JSON should be an object with a few of the following keys: street, city, state, postalCode, country and ISOCountryCode. For MacOS 10.12.4 or iOS 10.3, you can set subLocality and subAdministrativeArea, too.

parameters.name: ContactIdentifier
parameters.description: The contact identifier.

parameters.name: Label
parameters.description: The label to use. For your convenience we translate Work, Home and Other to the right values, so they get localized in display. Default label is Other.

parameters.name: JSON
parameters.description: The block of JSON.

functions.name: CNContact.SetValue

Selector can be birthday, contactRelations, dates, departmentName, emailAddresses, familyName, givenName, imageData, imageDataAvailable, instantMessageAddresses, jobTitle, middleName, namePrefix, nameSuffix, nickname, nonGregorianBirthday, organizationName, phoneNumbers, phoneticFamilyName, phoneticGivenName, phoneticMiddleName, phoneticOrganizationName, postalAddresses, previousFamilyName, socialProfiles, thumbnailImageData, note, type or urlAddresses. functions.name: Folders.UbiquityContainer
functions.description: Queries path for an iCloud container. Returns the path for the iCloud container associated with the specified identifier and establishes access to that container. You use this method to determine the location of your app’s ubiquity container directories and to configure your app’s initial iCloud access. The first time you call this method for a given ubiquity container, the system extends your app’s sandbox to include that container. In iOS, you must call this method at least once before trying to search for cloud-based files in the ubiquity container. If your app accesses multiple ubiquity containers, call this method once for each container. You can use the URL returned by this method to build paths to files and directories within your app’s ubiquity container. Each app that syncs documents to the cloud must have at least one associated ubiquity container in which to put those files. This container can be unique to the app or shared by multiple apps. Returns a path pointing to the specified ubiquity container, or "" if the container could not be located or if iCloud storage is unavailable for the current user or device. Calls URLForUbiquityContainerIdentifier in NSFileManager internally.

parameters.name: ContainerIdentifier
parameters.description: The fully-qualified container identifier for an iCloud container directory. The string you specify must not contain wildcards and must be of the form <TEAMID>.<CONTAINER>, where <TEAMID> is your development team ID and <CONTAINER> is the bundle identifier of the container you want to access. The container identifiers for your app must be declared in the com.apple.developer.ubiquity-container-identifiers array of the .entitlements property list file in your Xcode project. If you specify "" for this parameter, this method returns the first container listed in the com.apple.developer.ubiquity-container-identifiers entitlement array.

functions.name: Process.LoadLibrary
functions.description: Loads a given native library. This can be used to resolve dependencies with libraries in various places. This should work with .dll files on Windows, .dylib files on macOS and .so files on Linux. Windows error 193 means that 64-bit FileMaker tried to load 32-bit library or 32-bit FileMaker tried to load 64-bit library. The bit level must match between app and library. For macOS the error message will tell you about wrong architecture. If you like to interface with functions in the DLL, please use CFunction functions. If you have trouble with DLLs not loading on Windows, please check if you have new Visual Studio Runtime libraries installed. If you need more than one DLL, please use Process.SetDllDirectory to point to the folder to find the DLL files. On Linux if you get the error wrong ELF class: ELFCLASS32 if you try to load a 32-bit library into a 64-bit application. You may also get errors about version GLIBC_2.25 or similar if your libc library on the Linux installation isn't new enough for the loaded library. This function requires a native path. Use Path.FileMakerPathToNativePath to convert a FileMaker path to a native path if required. If you like to have the user choose the path, you can use FileDialog functions. For Server be aware that server has limited permissions and may not be able to access all files on a computer.

functions.name: Process.SetDllDirectory
functions.description: Adds a directory to the search path used to locate DLLs for the application. The directory to be added to the search path. If this parameter is an empty string, the call restores the default search order. The SetDllDirectory function affects all subsequent calls to the Process.LoadLibrary functions. It also effectively disables safe DLL search mode while the specified directory is in the search path. After calling SetDllDirectory, the standard DLL search path is: 1. The directory from which the application loaded. 2. The directory specified by the pathName parameter. 3. The system directory. Use the GetSystemDirectory function to get the path of this directory. The name of this directory is System32. 4. The 16-bit system directory. There is no function that obtains the path of this directory, but it is searched. The name of this directory is System. 5. The Windows directory. Use the GetWindowsDirectory function to get the path of this directory. 6. The directories that are listed in the PATH environment variable. Each time the SetDllDirectory function is called, it replaces the directory specified in the previous SetDllDirectory call.

parameters.name: Path
parameters.description: The new native path.

functions.name: QuickList.AddSQL

functions.description: Adds values to a quick list via SQL. All values in the result set are added as text to the list. Returns error in case of SQL error with error message. This function is currently only supported for FileMaker 11 and newer. If you need it for older versions, please contact us. This function takes variable number of parameters. Pass as much parameters as needed separated by the semicolon in FileMaker. Please repeat Params parameter as often as you need.

parameters.name: SQL Statement

parameters.name: Params...

functions.result: Returns number of items added or error.

parameters.name: List1

parameters.name: List2

parameters.name: Separator
parameters.description: The separator text. Can be multiple characters. For tab separated text, pass Char(9). For CSV separated text, pass ";" or ",".

parameters.name: Column
parameters.description: The index of the column to compare. Starts with 0 for first column.

parameters.name: ReturnNewList

functions.name: QuickList.BestMatch
functions.description: Looks for best match of a text in a list of texts. If not found, returns empty result, so FileMaker function isEmpty() will tell you if it's empty (instead of just having no text). Uses internally the Text.LevenshteinDistance function to compare all items and look for best match. If no entry matches over 50%, this may return empty text.

parameters.name: ListRef
parameters.description: The reference to the list returned from QuickList.New function.

parameters.name: SearchText
parameters.description: The text to search.

parameters.name: Flags
parameters.description: Pass 0 to use Levenshtein distance. Pass 1 to use Jaro-Winkler distance. Add 2 to return list of top 5 entries.

functions.result: Returns best match, empty or error.

functions.name: QuickList.FindDuplicateItems

functions.name: QuickList.FindEquals

functions.name: QuickList.FindUnequals

    </Value>
    <Repetition>
      <Calculation>1</Calculation>
    </Repetition>
    <Name>$json</Name>
  </Step>
  <Step enable="True" id="89" name="# (comment)">
    <Text> turn into a list</Text>
  </Step>
  <Step enable="True" id="141" name="Set Variable">
    <Value>
      <Calculation>MBS( "JSON.GetArrayItemsAsQuickList"; $json ) </Calculation>
    </Value>
    <Repetition>
      <Calculation>1</Calculation>
    </Repetition>
    <Name>$list</Name>
  </Step>
  <Step enable="True" id="89" name="# (comment)"/>
  <Step enable="True" id="89" name="# (comment)">
    <Text> now loop over entries to filter</Text>
  </Step>
  <Step enable="True" id="141" name="Set Variable">
    <Value>
      <Calculation>MBS( "QuickList.Count"; $list ) </Calculation>
    </Value>
    <Repetition>
      <Calculation>1</Calculation>
    </Repetition>
    <Name>$n</Name>
  </Step>
  <Step enable="True" id="68" name="If">
    <Restore state="False"/>
    <Calculation> $n > 0 </Calculation>
  </Step>
  <Step enable="True" id="71" name="Loop">
    <Restore state="False"/>
    <FlushType value="Always"/>
  </Step>
  <Step enable="True" id="89" name="# (comment)">
    <Text> get next item</Text>
  </Step>
  <Step enable="True" id="141" name="Set Variable">
    <Value>
      <Calculation>$n - 1 </Calculation>
    </Value>
    <Repetition>
      <Calculation>1</Calculation>
    </Repetition>
    <Name>$n</Name>
  </Step>
  <Step enable="True" id="141" name="Set Variable">
    <Value>
      <Calculation>MBS( "QuickList.GetValue"; $list; $n ) </Calculation>
    </Value>
    <Repetition>
      <Calculation>1</Calculation>
    </Repetition>
    <Name>$item</Name>
  </Step>
  <Step enable="True" id="89" name="# (comment)"/>
  <Step enable="True" id="89" name="# (comment)">
    <Text> if meets criteria, then remove it</Text>
  </Step>
  <Step enable="True" id="68" name="If">
    <Restore state="False"/>
    <Calculation> JSONGetElement ( $item ; "id" ) = 2 </Calculation>
  </Step>
  <Step enable="True" id="141" name="Set Variable">
    <Value>
      <Calculation>MBS( "QuickList.Remove"; $list; $n ) </Calculation>
    </Value>
    <Repetition>
      <Calculation>1</Calculation>
    </Repetition>
    <Name>$r</Name>
  </Step>
  <Step enable="True" id="70" name="End If"/>
  <Step enable="True" id="89" name="# (comment)"/>
  <Step enable="True" id="89" name="# (comment)">
    <Text> next</Text>
  </Step>
  <Step enable="True" id="72" name="Exit Loop If">
    <Calculation> $n ≤ 0 </Calculation>
  </Step>
  <Step enable="True" id="73" name="End Loop"/>
  <Step enable="True" id="70" name="End If"/>
  <Step enable="True" id="89" name="# (comment)"/>
  <Step enable="True" id="141" name="Set Variable">

    </Value>
    <Repetition>
      <Calculation>1</Calculation>
    </Repetition>
    <Name>$json</Name>
  </Step>
  <Step enable="True" id="87" name="Show Custom Dialog">

    </Title>
    <Message>
      <Calculation>$json </Calculation>
    </Message>
    <Buttons>

      </Button>
      <Button CommitState="False">
        <Calculation>"Cancel"</Calculation>
      </Button>
      <Button CommitState="False"/>
    </Buttons>
  </Step>
  <Step enable="True" id="89" name="# (comment)"/>
  <Step enable="True" id="141" name="Set Variable">

    </Value>
    <Repetition>
      <Calculation>1</Calculation>
    </Repetition>
    <Name>$r</Name>
  </Step>

functions.name: QuickList.New
functions.description: Creates a new list. You can provide whatever separator you need. Default is new line characters. But works also fine with comma, semicolon or tab characters. Please use QuickList.Release to release the list later. QuickList reference numbers are starting at 12000 and counting up for each new list. QuickLists can have multiple million of entries without problems. Just be aware of FileMaker's standard loop/recursion limit of 50000, which can be raised with SetRecursion function.

parameters.name: Text
parameters.description: Initial list content.

parameters.name: Separator
parameters.description: The separator to use. Can be ASCII character number (e.g. 9 for tab) or a text where we use first character as separator. Default is newline.

parameters.name: RefNum
parameters.description: The desired reference number. Leave empty for default.

functions.description: Returns values of both lists. Performs a logical OR operation. Checks the given column in both lists too compare. If Separator is empty, this is same as QuickList.Or , but slower.

parameters.name: List1
parameters.description: The reference to the first quicklist.

parameters.name: List2
parameters.description: The reference to the second quicklist.

parameters.name: Separator
parameters.description: The separator text. Can be multiple characters. For tab separated text, pass Char(9). For CSV separated text, pass ";" or ",".

parameters.name: Column
parameters.description: The index of the column to compare. Starts with 0 for first column.

parameters.name: ReturnNewList
parameters.description: Pass 1 to return result as new QuickList. This new list must be freed later using QuickList.Release function. Pass 0 (Default) to modify the list in the List1 parameter.

functions.name: QuickList.RegExMatch
functions.signature: MBS( "QuickList.RegExMatch"; ListRef; Pattern; CompilerOptions; ExecuteOptions { ; ReturnNewList } )
functions.description: Matches a list against a pattern. This compiles the pattern, executes it and looks if we have a match or not for each list item. Returns the list items which match.

parameters.name: ListRef
parameters.description: The reference to the list returned from QuickList.New function.

parameters.name: Pattern
parameters.description: The pattern to use.

parameters.name: CompilerOptions
parameters.description: A number for the options to use. e.g. 1 for case insensitive or 512 for ungreedy.

parameters.name: ExecuteOptions
parameters.description: The options for executing.

parameters.name: ReturnNewList
parameters.description: Pass 1 to return result as new QuickList. This new list must be freed later using QuickList.Release function. Pass 0 (Default) to modify the list in the List1 parameter.

functions.name: QuickList.Release
functions.description: Releases the list. Please call this for each list to make sure you don't run out of memory.

parameters.name: ListRef

functions.name: QuickList.Remove
functions.description: Removes the value with the given index.

parameters.name: ListRef

parameters.name: Index
parameters.description: The index of the item to remove. Range from 0 to QuickList.Count -1.

functions.name: QuickList.RemoveDuplicateItems
functions.description: Removes duplicate items in the list. Similar to UniqueValues function in FileMaker to find unique values.

parameters.name: ListRef
parameters.description: The reference to the list returned from QuickList.New function.

parameters.name: RemoveAll
parameters.description: If duplicate is found also remove the first occurrence. Set to 1 to enable or 0 to disable. Default is disabled.

parameters.name: ReturnNewList
parameters.description: Pass 1 to return result as new QuickList. This new list must be freed later using QuickList.Release function. Pass 0 (Default) to modify the list in the List1 parameter.

parameters.name: CaseInsensitive
parameters.description: Whether to perform comparison case insensitve. By default we do case sensitive operations, which are faster. Pass 1 for insensitve or 0 for sensitive.

functions.name: QuickList.RemoveEmptyItems
functions.description: Removes empty items in the list.

parameters.name: ListRef
parameters.description: The reference to the list returned from QuickList.New function.

functions.name: QuickList.RemovePostfix
functions.description: Removes a postfix text to each entry in the list.

parameters.name: ListRef
parameters.description: The reference to the list returned from QuickList.New function.

parameters.name: Postfix
parameters.description: The text to remove.

parameters.name: ReturnNewList
parameters.description: Pass 1 to return result as new QuickList. This new list must be freed later using QuickList.Release function. Pass 0 (Default) to modify the list in the List1 parameter.

parameters.name: CaseSensitive
parameters.description: Whether to match with case sensitive comparison. Default is 0 for case insensitive. You can pass 1 to have a case sensitive comparison.

functions.name: QuickList.Reserve

parameters.name: Size

functions.name: QuickList.Sort
functions.description: Sorts the list. Version 6.2 adds new modes for date sorting. Mode 4 for DD.MM.YYYY style and mode 8 for MM.DD.YYYY style. Add mode 16 for flags to sort by numbers for version 11.0.

parameters.name: ListRef
parameters.description: The reference to the list returned from QuickList.New function.

parameters.description: Optional, whether to sort case insensitive or descending. Pass 1 to sort case insensitive or 0 to sort case sensitive. Add 2 to sort descending. Add 4 for sorting dates in DD.MM.YYYY style and 8 for sorting dates in MM.DD.YYYY style.

functions.name: QuickList.SortWith
functions.description: Sorts the list with together with other lists. We sort the first list and move all items in other lists as well to match the order. You can pass as many lists in the parameters as needed, not just 2. Add mode 16 for flags to sort by numbers for version 11.0. This function takes variable number of parameters. Pass as much parameters as needed separated by the semicolon in FileMaker. Please repeat List2 parameter as often as you need.

parameters.name: ListRef
parameters.description: The reference to the list returned from QuickList.New function.

parameters.name: Flags
parameters.description: Optional, whether to sort case insensitive or descending. Pass 1 to sort case insensitive or 0 to sort case sensitive. Add 2 to sort descending. Add 4 for sorting dates in DD.MM.YYYY style and 8 for sorting dates in MM.DD.YYYY style. Add 16 to sort by numbers.

parameters.name: List1
parameters.description: The first list to sort with.

parameters.name: List2...
parameters.description: The second list to sort with.

functions.name: QuickList.SortWithEvaluate
functions.description: Sorts a list with using an expression to evaluate. The expression is run every time two values are compared, so keep it quick. It should return 1 if leftValue is smaller than rightValue. Our normal QuickList.Sort is faster due to not having the overhead of evaluating expressions.

parameters.name: ListRef
parameters.description: The reference to the list returned from QuickList.New function.

parameters.name: Expression
parameters.description: The expression to evaluate. Can include "leftValue" and "rightValue" as variables.

functions.name: QuickList.SubList
functions.signature: MBS( "QuickList.SubList"; ListRef; Index; Count { ; ReturnNewList; NoReturnEnding } )
functions.description: Returns a part of the list. Can return new QuickList or normal list.

parameters.name: ListRef
parameters.description: The reference to the list returned from QuickList.New function.

parameters.name: Index
parameters.description: The zero based index where to start. Or in other words: How many entries to skip.

parameters.name: Count
parameters.description: How many entries to copy. If negative, we pick the other items left.

parameters.name: ReturnNewList
parameters.description: Pass 1 to return result as new QuickList. This new list must be freed later using QuickList.Release function. Pass 0 (Default) to return a text list.

parameters.name: NoReturnEnding
parameters.description: If you passed 0 for ReturnNewList, decides about new list: Pass 1 to have no extra newline character on the end of the returned list. Default is 0 to include one to easily concat lists.

functions.name: QuickList.Trim
functions.description: Trims all texts in the list.

parameters.name: ListRef
parameters.description: The reference to the list returned from QuickList.New function.

functions.name: QuickList.ValueIndex
functions.description: Finds the index for a given value. Returns zero based index (0 = first list value). Returns empty result if not found. Comparison is case insensitive.

parameters.name: ListRef
parameters.description: The reference to the list returned from QuickList.New function.

parameters.name: Value
parameters.description: The text to find.

functions.name: QuickList.XOr
functions.description: Returns list with values found in either first or second list, but not in both. Performs an exclusive logical OR operation.

parameters.name: List1
parameters.description: The reference to the first quicklist.

parameters.name: List2
parameters.description: The reference to the second quicklist.

parameters.name: ReturnNewList
parameters.description: Pass 1 to return result as new QuickList. This new list must be freed later using QuickList.Release function. Pass 0 (Default) to modify the list in the List1 parameter.

functions.name: QuickList.XOrColumn
functions.signature: MBS( "QuickList.XOrColumn"; List1; List2; Separator; Column { ; ReturnNewList } )
functions.description: Returns list with values found in either first or second list, but not in both. Performs an exclusive logical OR operation. Checks the given column in both lists too compare. If Separator is empty, this is same as QuickList.XOr , but slower.

parameters.name: List1
parameters.description: The reference to the first quicklist.

parameters.name: List2
parameters.description: The reference to the second quicklist.

parameters.name: Separator
parameters.description: The separator text. Can be multiple characters. For tab separated text, pass Char(9). For CSV separated text, pass ";" or ",".

parameters.name: Column
parameters.description: The index of the column to compare. Starts with 0 for first column.

parameters.name: ReturnNewList
parameters.description: Pass 1 to return result as new QuickList. This new list must be freed later using QuickList.Release function. Pass 0 (Default) to modify the list in the List1 parameter.

functions.name: SchemaChange.Changes
functions.description: Queries the changes, that the plugin received. Calling this function clears the list and reports it back as JSON array. The plugin adds two fields "counter" and "timestamp" with the change counter and the current timestamp as text. You may have a scheduled script running on the server to react to changes. e.g. by using JSON.InsertRecord to add this to a log table or by running Save as XML script step to export the solution. This function only works in the server scripting process in FileMaker 21.1 or newer. The catalog value in the JSON may report one of these catalogs: custom function, custom menu set, data source, extended privilege, field, layout, script, privilege set, table, table alias, theme, user account, value list. New in FileMaker 26: persistent store. There may be more in the future. Result is "" if no changes are recorded. You need to call SchemaChange.Enable to enable the feature.
functions.result: Returns JSON array, empty or error.

examples.label: Sample script to log changes to records:
examples.text_code:
# check for pending changes
Set Variable [
$changes
; Value:
MBS
("SchemaChange.Changes") ]
#
# if we have changes, log them to a table
If [ Length (
$changes
) > 0 ]
Set Variable [
$r
; Value:
MBS
("
JSON.InsertRecords
"; Get(FileName); "SchemaChanges";
$changes
) ]
# table must have the following fields: account, catalog, file, id, user, basetableid, counter and time
End If

<fmxmlsnippet type="FMObjectList">
  <Step enable="True" id="89" name="# (comment)">
    <Text> check for pending changes</Text>
  </Step>
  <Step enable="True" id="141" name="Set Variable">
    <Value>
      <Calculation>MBS("SchemaChange.Changes") </Calculation>
    </Value>
    <Repetition>
      <Calculation>1</Calculation>
    </Repetition>
    <Name>$changes</Name>
  </Step>
  <Step enable="True" id="89" name="# (comment)"/>
  <Step enable="True" id="89" name="# (comment)">
    <Text> if we have changes, log them to a table</Text>
  </Step>
  <Step enable="True" id="68" name="If">
    <Restore state="False"/>
    <Calculation> Length ( $changes ) > 0 </Calculation>
  </Step>
  <Step enable="True" id="141" name="Set Variable">
    <Value>
      <Calculation>MBS("JSON.InsertRecords"; Get(FileName); "SchemaChanges"; $changes) </Calculation>
    </Value>
    <Repetition>
      <Calculation>1</Calculation>
    </Repetition>
    <Name>$r</Name>
  </Step>
  <Step enable="True" id="89" name="# (comment)">
    <Text> table must have the following fields: account, catalog, file, id, user, basetableid, counter and time</Text>
  </Step>
  <Step enable="True" id="70" name="End If"/>
</fmxmlsnippet>

functions.name: SerialPort.Open
functions.description: Opens a serial port. You get the names from SerialPort.List function. You can even open ports, if they are not in the list. The port is opened with default settings. Serial Port reference numbers are starting at 28000 and counting up for each new port. Even if port is not showing in list, it may still open here, e.g. virtual COM ports on Windows. You can open several ports with different connections, e.g. by calling SerialPort.Open once for each connection. Version 9.2 introduced a workaround to make this work for port numbers > COM9 on Windows.

parameters.name: Index

Go to Layout [ “MPO201 Input Weight” (MPORawMaterialColourInputs_MPO RM inputs) ]
Set Variable [
$portList
; Value:
MBS
("
SerialPort.List
") ]
Show Custom Dialog [ Title: "Serial Ports"; Message:
$portList
; Default Button: “OK”, Commit: “Yes”; Button 2: “Cancel”, Commit: “No” ]
If [ Get ( LastMessageChoice ) = 2 ]
Exit Script [ ]
End If
#Change to reflect actual COM port
Set Variable [
$port
; Value:"COM4" ]
Set Variable [
$serialPort
; Value:
MBS
("SerialPort.Open";
$port
) ]
If [
MBS
("IsError") ]
Show Custom Dialog [ Title: "Error"; Message: "Serial port error " &
$serialPort
; Default Button: “OK”, Commit: “Yes” ]
Exit Script [ ]
End If
Set Variable [
$baudSet
; Value:
MBS
("
SerialPort.SetBaudRate
";
$serialPort
; 9600) ]
Set Variable [
$count
; Value:0 ]
// New Record/Request
Loop
Set Variable [
$newScaleData
; Value:
MBS
("
SerialPort.Read
";
$serialPort
; 1000) ]
Exit Loop If [
$newScaleData
≠ "" ]
Exit Loop If [
$count
> 100 ]
Pause/Resume Script [ Duration (seconds): .01 ]
Set Variable [
$count
; Value:
$count
+ 1 ]
End Loop
#Change to reflect fields
Set Field [
MPORawMaterialColourInputs_MPO RM inputs::mpoiw
Input Weight Grams;
$newScaleData
]
Set Field [
MPORawMaterialColourInputs_MPO RM inputs::mpoiw
Input Weight Grams; Trim ( Left (
$newScaleData
; 9) ) ]
Commit Records/Requests
Set Variable [
$result
; Value:
MBS
("
SerialPort.Close
";
$serialPort
) ]
If [
MBS
("IsError") ]
Show Custom Dialog [ Title: "Error"; Message: "Serial port error " &
$result
; Default Button: “OK”, Commit: “Yes” ]
Else
Show Custom Dialog [ Title: "Info"; Message: "Serial port closed " &
$result
; Default Button: “OK”, Commit: “Yes” ]
End If

functions.name: SerialPort.OpenPath
functions.description: Opens a special file, device or pipe. This allows you to e.g. open a pipe on Windows. Serial Port reference numbers are starting at 28000 and counting up for each new port.

parameters.name: Path
parameters.description: The native path to open.

parameters.name: Mode
parameters.description: The opening mode. Can be Read, Write or ReadWrite. Default is ReadWrite.

functions.result: Returns the port reference value which you pass to other SerialPort functions.

functions.name: SerialPort.Path
functions.description: Queries the path used to open the serial port. This is the value passed to SerialPort.Open function. Value is e.g. "COM1"

parameters.name: PortReference
parameters.description: The reference number of the port. You get this number from SerialPort.Open when you open the port.

functions.name: SerialPort.Read
functions.description: Reads bytes from serial port and returns them as text. The text returned may be shorter than length bytes. You may need to put in script pauses between sending a request and reading the response as the other device may need a second to process the request, answer and for the answer to be received. See also SerialPort.AvailableBytes function. The script trigger pauses after it triggered a script and waits for you to call a function to read. This function clears the flag and allows the script trigger to fire again.

parameters.name: PortReference
parameters.description: The reference number of the port. You get this number from SerialPort.Open when you open the port.

parameters.name: Length
parameters.description: Maximum number of bytes to read.

parameters.name: Encoding
parameters.description: The text encoding for result. Default is native. This function can also handle UTF-16 as well as UTF-16LE and UTF-16BE for little/big endian byte order. Possible encoding names: ANSI, ISO-8859-1, Latin1, Mac, Native, UTF-8, DOS, Hex, Base64 or Windows. More listed in the FAQ .

functions.name: SerialPort.SetDataAvailableHandler
functions.description: Sets the data available handler for this serial port. When new data arrives, this script is called, so you can call SerialPort.Read functions. We pass the port reference as parameter to the script. Be aware that script may be called when just a few bytes are in the read buffer. So the data message you wait for may only be available partly. In that case, please read available bytes, check if whole packet/message arrived and if not, store read data for later and wait for next script call. With plugin version 6.0 or newer the script name can be a script ID number. In that case the plugin queries the script name for the given script ID. This allows to call scripts by ID and avoid problems if scripts are later renamed. Notice: FileMaker 19.2 adds a fmplugin extended privileges. If you have such an extended privileges to allow the plugin to trigger scripts, you need to grant permissions for it. If such a privilege is not defined, the plugin is allowed to trigger scripts. See FileMaker product documentation for details.

functions.name: ServiceProvider.Install
functions.description: Installs a service provider handler. If you add right info.plist entries to the info.plist inside the FileMaker app, you register services. The plugin starts a script when a service request is received. Best call this function in the script called when solutions opens. This function has been verified to work well for file and text services. Other types are also implemented, but not tested. see also: https://developer.apple.com/library/mac/documentation/Cocoa/Conceptual/SysServices/introduction.html With plugin version 6.0 or newer the script name can be a script ID number. In that case the plugin queries the script name for the given script ID. This allows to call scripts by ID and avoid problems if scripts are later renamed. Notice: FileMaker 19.2 adds a fmplugin extended privileges. If you have such an extended privileges to allow the plugin to trigger scripts, you need to grant permissions for it. If such a privilege is not defined, the plugin is allowed to trigger scripts. See FileMaker product documentation for details.

functions.name: TextView.CreateWithControl
functions.description: Creates a new text view on the given window covering the area of the given control. Use TextView.Release later to destroy the text view. If you use a register (tab controls) on the window, be aware that the text view actually is in front of the register (tab controls). You may hide the text view if another register is visible. Text view reference numbers are starting at 81000 and counting up for each new text view. When creating on a card window, please pass reference to parent window or just 0 for front window. On MacOS you may need to pass delta y value to adjust position. If you create a control on a new window, you may do window update command in your script first to have FileMaker actually build the window with controls and display it. A short script pause or using FM.RunScriptLater with 0.1 delay can help having all controls draw themselves. Then you can use this command to put our control on top. We use GetLayoutObjectAttribute() to query left, top, width and height and this gives empty value if control is not yet here. Creation fails to pick the right window in case the window is selected by name and the window name is not unique. In that case better work with window reference numbers or just pass 0 for current front window.

But with Twain.GetFilePaths you can learn where files have been stored. The path must end with a slash on Mac and a backslash on Windows. This function requires a native path. Use Path.FileMakerPathToNativePath to convert a FileMaker path to a native path if required. If you like to have the user choose the path, you can use FileDialog functions.

Whether lighter values are smaller or larger can be determined by examining the Current value of PixelFlavor. If more or less than 8 bits are used to describe the image, the actual data values should be normalized to fit within the 0-255 range. Notice: FileMaker 19.2 adds a fmplugin extended privileges. If you have such an extended privileges to allow the plugin to trigger scripts, you need to grant permissions for it. The normalization need not result in a homogeneous distribution if the original distribution was not homogeneous. Plugin uses value -10000 for undefined/default.

functions.name: USB.Count
functions.description: Queries all USB Devices and returns the number of found devices. This function must be called before all the other USB functions to initialize the plugin and to refresh the USB device list.

examples.label: Query number of devices
examples.text_code:
MBS
( "USB.Count" )
Query number of devices
examples.xml_code:

<fmxmlsnippet type="FMObjectList">
  <Step enable="True" id="141" name="Set Variable">
    <Value>
      <Calculation>MBS( "USB.Count" )</Calculation>
    </Value>
    <Repetition>
      <Calculation>1</Calculation>
    </Repetition>
    <Name>$r</Name>
  </Step>
</fmxmlsnippet>

functions.name: USB.FindDevice
functions.description: Finds USB devices. Please call USB.Count before you use this function. Pass IDs for vendor and product. e.g. Apple has vendor ID 1452 (hex 05ac). An Apple keyboard can have a product ID of 545 (hex 0221). Please note that product and vendor IDs are shown usually as hexadecimal values.

parameters.name: VendorID
parameters.description: The vendor ID of the device to find. Typically a number between 1 and 65535.

parameters.name: ProductID
parameters.description: The product ID of the device. Typically a number between 1 and 65535.

functions.result: The index of the device in our USB device list.

examples.label: Find a device and query it's product name:
examples.text_code:
$count
=
MBS
( "
USB.Count
" )
$index
=
MBS
( "USB.FindDevice";
$VendorID
;
$ProductID
)
$name
=
MBS
( "
USB.GetProductName
";
$index
)
Find a device and query it's product name:
examples.xml_code:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<fmxmlsnippet type="FMObjectList">
  <Step enable="True" id="141" name="Set Variable">
    <Value>
      <Calculation>MBS( "USB.Count" )</Calculation>
    </Value>
    <Repetition>
      <Calculation>1</Calculation>
    </Repetition>
    <Name>$count</Name>
  </Step>
  <Step enable="True" id="141" name="Set Variable">

    </Repetition>
    <Name>$index</Name>
  </Step>
  <Step enable="True" id="141" name="Set Variable">

      <Calculation>MBS( "USB.GetProductName"; $index )</Calculation>
    </Value>
    <Repetition>
      <Calculation>1</Calculation>
    </Repetition>
    <Name>$name</Name>
  </Step>
</fmxmlsnippet>
